recipes.name: Soft Oatmeal Cookies
ingredients_raw: 2 tablespoons white sugar, or as needed

steps.text: Whisk flour, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt together in a medium bowl until well combined.
Beat butter, 1 cup white sugar, and brown sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer until creamy, at least 2 to 3 minutes.
Beat in eggs, one at a time, then mix in vanilla.
Gradually mix in dry ingredients until well combined. Add oats and mix until thoroughly incorporated. Cover the bowl and chill dough in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.

When ready to bake, preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Spray two cookie sheets with floured cooking spray. Place water in a small bowl and 2 tablespoons sugar in another small bowl. Roll chilled dough into walnut-sized balls, and place 2 inches apart on the prepared cookie sheets. Dip a large fork in water, then in sugar, and use to flatten each cookie, rewetting and resugaring as necessary.
Bake in the preheated oven until light golden brown around the edges and centers are nearly set, 8 to 10 minutes, switching racks halfway through.
Allow cookies to cool on baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Soft Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: Oatmeal cookies are a family-favorite and this classic recipe is a winner, producing soft, chewy oatmeal cookies with just a hint of cinnamon flavor.

video.description: Endlessly customizable and perfect for the holidays, these homemade cookies bring a feeling of comfort with every bite. In this video, learn how to make soft and easy oatmeal cookies with the Allrecipes team. In only an hour, these chewy desserts are ready to serve.

review.reviewBody: These were fantastic, but NOT moist! First, you do not need to dip the fork in sugar when you press these cookies flat. They are sweet enough! Don't press the cookies flat if you don't like thin & crispy cookies. Leave them in little balls for thicker and more chewy cookies. Finally, I added 1/2 cup of chopped walnuts to the batter and then divided it into 3 bowls. In one, I added 1/3 cup of raisins, in another, 1/3 cup of semi-sweet chocolate chips, and in the last one, I added 1/4 cup of dried cranberries and 1/4 cup of shredded coconut. They needed a full 10 minutes to bake and they were all DELICIOUS!!!

Wow! I loved these cookies and they were super easy to make. I used Splenda instead of sugar. WW flour in place pf white flour and added raisins. I also took the advice of another eviewer and left them round instead of flattening them with a fork and the came out round, soft and perfect. I will make these again and again. Thanks for the great recipe.

This is the best oatmeal cookie recipe I've had yet. I can't put my finger on what separates this one from the rest, but the ingredients are the perfect combination for a great tasting cookie. Crispy on the edges and soft and chewy in the middle, with a perfect blend of spices. I can't wait to try them with raisins and various flavors of chips (chocolate, butterscotch, and cinnamon). Thanks for a great recipe.

The perfect oatmeal cookie. No rocket science here--simple to mix, simple to bake, great results. Bake longer for chewier, shorter time for softer cookies, add nuts or raisins if you like or just as is. Nice oatmeal flavor with just a hint of cinnamon and not overshadowed by a ton of spices. Just that simple.

My family loved it!! I’m currently breastfeeding and I added 1 tbsp of brewers yeast and I subbed the white and brown sugar with coconut sugar. I also baked the cookies for 12 minutes instead of the recommended 8 - 10 minutes for a soft yet crunchy cookie. It turned out to be one of my favorite lactation cookies I’ve made so far! The coconuts sugar gave the cookie a more caramel taste to it. I’ve also noticed that if I do not leave it in the fridge to cool for at least an hour or so, it’ll spread. So I left it in the fridge for about two hours and it baked well.
I used the recipe and added a cup of craisins, cup of chocolate chips, cup of coconut, cup of pecans, and a cup of peanut butter chips. Always good , my go to everything recipe

I cut the white sugar by 1/3 cup and didn’t dip the fork in sugar since so many people reviewing the recipe said the recipe was too sweet. I also increased the ground cinnamon to 2 tsp. I made each cookie dough ball slightly smaller than a walnut. I liked the way they turned out and my family liked them too.

Choose this recipe because it says soft oatmeal and it really is! Halved the recipe to test it out and they're great. Super easy, I added chocolate chips, didn't have to refrigerate or roll them just used 2 teaspoons to make tiny cookies and dropped cooking time to 7min. 👌🏽 Keeping this recipe !

I usually love most All Recipes but these cookies were disappointing. They are WAY too sweet. I usually can't resist eating 2-3 cookies when they are warm out of the oven but these were so sweet that I didn't even enjoy one. My son didn't like them either. The sugar could be cut in half. I would suggest 3/4 cup of brown sugar and 1/4 cup of white sugar. I would also leave out the cinnamon. The Quaker recipe is much better than this one.

Y'all, EVERYONE in my house absolutely loves this recipe! Now, I did heavily doctor it up to make it a true, genuinely homemade treat, which means this Southern mama didn't follow the original directions too closely. Bless it, these turned into the most beautiful golden-brown, buttery oatmeal raisin cookies you ever did see! They are so popular around here that I barely get to taste my own baking before the plate is licked clean. To fix a little bit of a salty taste from my first couple of batches, I went ahead and tossed in about half a box (2 whole cups!) of plump raisins. I also swapped out the quick oats for rolled oats. Honey, it made them perfectly crisp on the outside and wonderfully chewy on the inside. That complex flavor was just absolute perfection for my family. I also added a tablespoon of my precious homemade vanilla extract—bless its heart, it has been sitting and aging on my shelf for nearly two years now! Finally, I cut way back on the sugar to make them safe and friendly for my sweet diabetic mama and daddy. They just loved them to pieces, and you couldn't even tell there was barely a pinch of sugar in the bowl. I will be baking these cookies again and again, y'all. I fully plan on passing this special homemade version down to my children and their children someday!

This was su a simple recipe! I added and extra teaspoon of vanilla and substituted the oats for some lemon creme and blueberry instant oatmeal packets (in the same quantities of course lol). They came out AMAZING!! I opted to not do the sugar press with the fork and instead made the dough into balls and flattened them a bit with my hands to like a burger patty thickness.
Husband approved! Finally found an oatmeal cookie recipe he loved!

These cookies turned out amazing. Chewy and great without any raisins, nuts, or chips added. They were a pain to mix together but very much worth the effort. Im glad I did not add anything because they are perfectly sweet just the way they are
Too sweet and flat.
Always our Family favorite for Friday movie nights

Followed the recipe but added 1/2 bag choc chips and 1 cup walnuts. Did not chill before baking. Bake the first batch at 375 and I was afraid they were getting done on the edges and not in the middle so the next couple pants I did at 350. I didn’t care for the way they looked so I went back to 375 but they taste wonderful
very nice, a sprinkle of chocolate chips would 100% elevate this recipe
Love it it
It was delicious, I also made ice cream sandwiches with them

I added white almond bark in small chunks to the batter. Very yummy. Probably the best recipe I’ve ever made and I’m 74 years old and have a big family, so I have made them many times. The best. Thank you again.
